top_examples.text:
Introduction
============

Medications that modulate serotoninergic neurotransmission, like selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs), are commonly prescribed to treat depression, anxiety disorders, and premenstrual dysphoria,[@b1-dhps-5-211] as well as chronic pain conditions. During the past decade, numerous reports have been published on the risk of abnormal gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding as an infrequent adverse event (AE) associated with serotonin-modulating drugs.[@b2-dhps-5-211] Patients with musculoskeletal pain conditions, as well as patients with depression and anxiety who experience chronic pain, may also be treated with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) including aspirin, which are also associated with GI bleeding.[@b3-dhps-5-211],[@b4-dhps-5-211] Concomitant use of NSAIDs with SSRIs or SNRIs may potentiate bleeding-related AEs.[@b5-dhps-5-211]

The tendency for GI bleeding during treatment with serotonin-modulating drugs is linked to a decrease in blood platelet function that is dependent on serotonin. Platelets release serotonin at sites of vascular injury, which signals vasoconstriction and amplification of platelet aggregation for hemostatic thrombus formation.[@b6-dhps-5-211] However, platelets accumulate serotonin via transporters.[@b7-dhps-5-211] Treatment with therapeutic doses of serotonin-modulating agents blocks these transporters,[@b8-dhps-5-211] ultimately impairing serotonin accumulation and thereby rendering platelets dysfunctional.

Duloxetine (Cymbalta®; Eli Lilly and Company, Indianapolis, IN, USA) is an SNRI that is approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for the treatment of major depressive disorder and generalized anxiety disorder and the management of neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy, fibromyalgia, and chronic musculoskeletal pain associated with osteoarthritis and chronic low back pain. Outside of the United States, it is also approved for lower urinary tract disorders in some countries. A safety profile of duloxetine across these indications has been published that analyzed rates of common treatment-emergent AEs (TEAEs) (defined as AEs that were experienced by 5% or more of duloxetine-treated patients) comparing duloxetine with placebo.[@b9-dhps-5-211] In those analyses, the frequency of any single bleeding-related event did not meet the threshold for being classified as a common TEAE. The objective of the current analyses was to gain a better understanding of the risk of bleeding-related TEAEs associated with duloxetine treatment in patients who used concomitant NSAIDs. We analyzed the incidence of these TEAEs from placebo-controlled trials of duloxetine across indications. In addition, we analyzed the incidence of these events reported in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS), which receives reports from health care professionals, consumers, and pharmaceutical manufacturers.

Folk music refers to the traditional music of a society or a region, often passed down through generations and reflecting the cultural heritage, beliefs and practices of the community. Folk music has its origins in various parts of the world and has developed over time, influenced by political, social, and economic factors.

One of the earliest forms of folk music can be traced back to the ancient tradition of oral storytelling. In Africa, Griots, or wandering musicians and poets, sang songs and told stories about their ancestors and history, passing on important cultural knowledge to future generations.

In Europe, folk music developed in various forms, such as ballads, work songs, and dance music. These musical genres were often sung by the peasantry and working classes and reflected their daily lives, such as heartbreak, love, labor, and strife.

The advent of colonization and the slave trade brought about new forms of folk music in the Americas. African slaves in North and South America used music as a way to communicate and express their emotions and spiritual beliefs. They created early forms of blues, jazz, and gospel music, which later influenced other musical styles such as rock and roll, hip-hop, and rap.

Similarly, the Irish and Scottish immigrants who settled in America brought with them the traditional music of their homeland, which later evolved into country and western music.

In Asia, the traditional music of India, China, and Japan has been passed down through generations and is characterized by unique instruments and melodic structures. Indian classical music, for example, consists of intricate rhythms and melodies and is often associated with religious and spiritual practices.

Throughout history, folk music has played an important role in shaping the cultural identities of different societies. It has been used as a means of resistance against colonialism and oppression, as well as a tool for building community and fostering social change.

In contemporary times, folk music continues to influence popular music genres and serves as a means of cultural preservation and celebration. Many popular music artists, such as Bob Dylan, Joan Baez, and Pete Seeger, have incorporated folk music elements into their work and helped to popularize the genre.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger verbs and quantity words (analyzed, median, showed, investigate, determine) in a sports coaching context; hypothesis predicts far less firing outside biomedicine.

The median bake time settled near forty minutes, and we analyzed crumb photos to rank the starters.
